newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil recovers some earlier losses.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil recovers some earlier losses.

text.p: NWE high and low sulphur fuel oil prices recovered some losses on Wednesday after Italian buying on Tuesday and amid good bunker demand on Wednesday, traders said.

High sulphur barges traded at $96 a tonne fob ARA in the morning then rose steadily. Bunker demand was "pretty steamy," according to one trader. The highest trade was at $100, near the end of business.
High sulphur cargo offers rose too. Utilities reported offers at around $99/$100 but buying was pegged two or three dollars lower.
Low sulphur fuel was firmer. An Italian utility was thought to have bought two cargoes on Tuesday, at least one of which was from a trader.
One of the deals was heard done at around $118/$119 cif Italy.

A French refiner also bought a small low sulphur piece on Tuesday at a floating price, to cover increased local demand. But buying on Wednesday was thin. February swaps spent much of the day at around $107/$108 fob NWE.
Physical offers into Italy were heard at $119 cif.
